status_meaning.works: Re-checked from a fresh clone: it builds, runs and reproduces the numbers in its README.
status_meaning.partly: The code and recorded proof are public; the note says which part is not reproducible from outside yet.

demos.name: References: anything to anything
demos.line: One kind of name reaches a file on a laptop, a blob, a repo file at a commit, a node, a person, a cell op, a capability and an enterprise system. It follows moves and refuses changed bytes.
demos.note: A fresh clone runs four devices and eight steps: 9 of 9 kinds resolved, 2 of 2 tampered files refused, 3 of 3 offline resolves, 60 of 60 ids byte-identical. A live system.

demos.name: Render across devices
demos.line: One image, rendered by several machines at once. The result is pixel-identical to a single-machine render.
demos.note: A fresh clone renders the reference and the tiled frame (one tile killed and retried) to the same hash.

demos.name: Kill a node, keep the data
demos.line: Kill the server holding the data, live. Every saved write survives, and the page proves it with a hash chain.
demos.note: A fresh clone passes the local failover test: 3 leader kills, 351 acknowledged writes, every proof holds.

demos.name: An engineering result you can re-check
demos.line: A physics result that comes with a certificate. Re-check it in your own browser: same code, same inputs, same answer.
demos.note: A fresh clone verifies all 5 certificates and rejects 440 of 440 tampered edits.

demos.name: One prompt, many devices
demos.line: Ask a question and see which device answers. When one device drops out, the answer keeps streaming from another.
demos.note: The recorded run is in the repo (98 tokens, 98 of 98 signatures valid, switch at token 12). The live two-device page is not public yet.

demos.name: Follow-me cell
demos.line: A service that moves to whichever machine is closest to you, and keeps answering by the same name while it moves.
demos.note: The restart on one device is recorded. A recorded move between two devices is not in the repo yet.

demos.name: Playground: deploy a cell in your browser
demos.line: Write a cell in your browser, deploy it to a real network, and call it from three languages, all within a minute.
demos.note: Code and tests for the sandbox, fuel limit and refusals are public. The hosted playground is not live yet.

demos.name: A stranger gets exactly one action
demos.line: We give you a key that does exactly one thing. Try to make it do more. Every attempt is refused, and the page shows you the rule that refused it.
demos.note: The build needs a protocol crate that is not published yet, so the tests cannot run from outside.

demos.name: Same data, browser and terminal, live
demos.line: Change a value in your browser and see it change in a terminal and on a 3D factory map at the same moment. One schema, no server code.
demos.note: Recorded logs show 23 and 18 ms end to end and the same type error in both SDKs. Not yet re-run from a fresh clone.

demos.name: Search everything you are allowed to see
demos.line: One search box across many machines. You only get back what your key allows, and the rest never leaves the machine it lives on.
demos.note: The recorded report is in the repo (guest key 11 to 6 hits, engineer key 11 to 11). The build needs crates that are not published yet.

demos.name: Any program becomes a mesh service in one command
demos.line: Turn any open-source program into a network service with one command. Then use it from your browser: same output, byte for byte.
demos.note: Tests pass and a local run reproduces the recorded output hash. Parity across machines is not re-checked, and one dependency is not public yet.

demos.name: Print only through the guard
demos.line: Send a print job straight to the printer and it is refused. Send it through the guard, which checks bounds, temperatures, material and time: the 300 C job is rejected, the safe one prints, and a replay is refused.
demos.note: Fresh clone: 4 attempts, 3 refused with the rule that decided, 40 of 40 layers streamed; report matches byte for byte.

demos.name: Every call leaves a receipt
demos.line: Run 200 calls across four cells, download the receipts, and check them on any machine with no network. Edit one and the verifier names it; drop one and the chain shows the gap.
demos.note: A fresh clone reproduces the 200 receipts byte for byte: 200 of 200 valid, and the tampered and gapped files fail. CI checks it offline.

demos.name: Shared with my devices, nobody else's
demos.line: Enroll your laptop, phone and desktop with a pairing code; each gets a key bound to that device. A copied key file is refused, and a lost phone is revoked from the laptop while the other two keep working.
demos.note: Fresh clone: 3 devices accepted, the copied key refused by the holder proof, the revoked phone refused 81 ms after the revoke; 11 of 11 golden vectors pass ce-net-capability-verify.

demos.name: Sharded search: one leader per shard, rebalanced live
demos.line: 4.6 million Wikipedia abstracts in 32 shards with 3 replicas each, one leader per shard. Kill a machine under a query loop that never stops: new leaders within one lease, replicas back to three, recall unchanged.
demos.note: Recorded run: 96 instances, 7 leaders lost with machine-c, new leaders within 3.65 s, all shards back to 3 replicas in 6.57 s, 0 failed queries, recall@10 0.9202 before and after. All machines are processes on one server; the ce-net crates it was designed around are replaced by public stand-ins.

demos.name: A factory line you can audit
demos.line: A three-station line runs as a twin and drill becomes the bottleneck. Download the signed event log: your browser checks every signature and recomputes the numbers. Edit one timestamp and it names the event that broke.
demos.note: Fresh clone: seed 42 reproduces the committed log byte for byte, 320 of 320 signatures verify, the tampered file fails on event 116 (drill).

demos.name: A cell that takes its data with it
demos.line: A notes cell moves from process A to process B while a client writes to it 20 times a second. B takes over under a higher epoch, A answers stale writes with 'moved, epoch 2', and writes sent, acknowledged and present all match.
demos.note: Fresh clone builds in under a minute; recorded 10 moves at 20 writes/s and 100 moves at 1600 writes/s with 0 writes lost or duplicated and the same hash-chain head on both sides. CI repeats the 100 moves on every push (median freeze 0.65 ms).

demos.name: Read it before you can act
demos.line: An approve key that only works after your device signs a read receipt for the exact notice. Approve first and it is refused with the clause that refused it; open the notice and the same call goes through.
demos.note: Fresh clone: call 1 refused by the require read clause, receipt signed, call 3 (same request) accepted, a fresh verifier agrees; 13 of 13 golden vectors pass ce-net-capability-verify offline.

demos.name: Edit offline, merge on reconnect
demos.line: A laptop and a phone share a parts list. Pull the cable, edit both sides, plug it back in: both show the same list within a second, the page shows how each conflict was resolved, and both state hashes match.
demos.note: Fresh clone with empty caches: all five partition scenarios pass in 109 s. Rust and TypeScript replica processes, in every pairing, write byte-identical op logs and reach the golden state hash (db-conformance M1-M5); CI re-checks on every push.

demos.name: A key with a spending limit
demos.line: Give an agent a key worth 100 units and three cells that cost different amounts. A live meter drops with each call; at 3 left a 5-unit call is refused by a cell that has never seen the key, and splitting the key into two keys worth 100 each is refused.
demos.note: Fresh clone builds and runs in under a minute: 13 debits to 3 of 100 left, the 5-unit resize and both splits refused. CI fires 10 concurrent clients in 5 rounds; total spend never exceeds 100.

demos.name: Work that pays only when it checks out
demos.line: A requester posts 50 jobs and two workers take them; one is rigged to answer wrong one time in ten. A cheap verifier checks every result, only a pass gets a signed single-use reward token, and the rigged worker's acceptance rate drops live.
demos.note: Fresh clone: seed 68 replays the committed report byte for byte; 47 of 50 results paid, all 3 injected wrong answers (one hash, one sort, one solve) rejected, every token verifies and pays once.

demos.name: Revoke once, refused everywhere
demos.line: Six cells accept one delegated key. Press revoke and each cell turns red as it refuses, with the milliseconds since the revoke. A cut-off cell keeps serving until its 30 s freshness bound runs out, then refuses everything.
demos.note: Fresh clone: 20 recorded runs, connected cells refuse at p50 1.2 to 1.8 ms (max 30.1 ms), the cut-off cell at 29.9 s max, 0 accepts after max(propagation, 30 s bound).

demos.name: One struct, three nodes
demos.line: One Rust struct becomes a typed Rust client and a generated TypeScript client. Kill one of three nodes mid-run: no write is lost, offline edits merge, two viewers see different rows, and a renamed field fails to compile in both languages.
demos.note: Fresh clone (CI): 1,000 writes with node c killed at 300 and back at 700, 0 lost; 50 of 50 offline conflicts resolved, 0 rows off the reference merge; every proof step signed.

demos.name: Fundamentals, live
demos.line: Ten fundamental cells on a four-node mesh: typed contracts, by_name, ce-gate, cap v3 with Via, state.store, failover, search, orch, pinned builds and wrap. Every call is a signed record.
demos.note: The recorded run verifies offline from a fresh clone and the page replays it; running the mesh yourself needs read access to private ce-net cells.
